lessons.title: What is a foul
lessons.objective: You can explain what makes contact a foul and what the restart is.

payload.prompt: A defender kicks the attacker's leg while going for the ball. Foul?

scene.alt: A defender's foot makes contact with an attacker's leg; the defender did not get the ball first.

explanation.correct: Yes. If the defender's leg catches the attacker without getting the ball first, that's careless contact and a foul.
explanation.incorrect: Contact that is careless or reckless without getting the ball is a foul. Effort counts if you get the ball clean.
explanation.sayThisLine: Didn't get the ball, just took the leg. That's a foul.

payload.prompt: After a foul in the opponent's penalty area, what is the restart?

options.text: Indirect free kick
Direct free kick
Penalty kick

explanation.correct: Right. A foul in the box is a penalty, a one-on-one from the spot.
explanation.incorrect: Fouls inside the penalty area give a penalty kick, not a free kick. That's the highest punishment for contact.
explanation.sayThisLine: In the box, it's a penalty. Outside, it's a free kick.

payload.prompt: A striker pushes a centre-back in the back with both hands. Foul?

scene.alt: A forward extends both arms and pushes a defender in the shoulders from behind while neither is competing for the ball.

explanation.correct: Yes. Pushing without the ball is excessive force, a foul every time.
explanation.incorrect: Any push away from the ball is a foul. Excessive force is the rule, and pushing is excessive.
explanation.sayThisLine: No contact away from the ball, that's the rule.

payload.prompt: Can you score straight from a direct free kick?

options.text: Yes, straight into the net counts
No, another player must touch it first
Only if it's outside the box

explanation.correct: Right. Direct free kicks can go straight in; the name is the clue.
explanation.incorrect: A direct free kick can score straight into the goal. The distinction is in the name: direct vs indirect.
explanation.sayThisLine: Direct free kicks go straight in if you bend it right.

payload.prompt: A defender's hand touches the ball on purpose while trying to stop a shot. Foul?

scene.alt: A defender deliberately puts a hand in front of a shot attempt to block it; the hand contact is clear and intentional.

explanation.correct: Yes. Deliberate handball is a foul, and in the box it's a penalty.
explanation.incorrect: Any deliberate use of the hand to play the ball is a foul. The arm is the rule.
explanation.sayThisLine: Hand ball stops, it's always a foul.

payload.prompt: A defender's leg trips an attacker who is running away. Is it a foul?

options.text: No, he was running away so it's not serious
Yes, any trip is a foul regardless of direction
Only if the defender meant it

explanation.correct: Right. A trip is a foul whether the attacker is coming at you or running away.
explanation.incorrect: Any trip is a foul. The direction does not matter; the contact does.
explanation.sayThisLine: Tripped is tripped, that's the rule.

statement.speaker: Jamie
statement.text: That wasn't even contact, he just slowed down.

payload.question: What does Jamie think?

options.text: There was no contact so there's no foul
The referee made a bad call
Someone fouled someone
It was a careless kick

payload.translation: Jamie is saying the contact was minimal or didn't happen, so it shouldn't have been called a foul.

followUps.line: Did it look like a dive to you?
followUps.why: Asks if the attacker exaggerated contact.

followUps.line: Did you see the contact in slow motion?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you didn't see the contact clearly, ask what Jamie saw.

lessons.title: Yellow, red and second yellow
lessons.objective: You can explain the difference between a caution and a sending-off.

payload.prompt: Match the card to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A caution for bad behaviour; two yellows in one match mean a red and a sending-off.
A sending-off for serious foul play or violent conduct; the player is off immediately.
A second caution in the same match results in a red and the player leaves the field.

explanation.summary: Yellow warns; two yellows or one serious offence and the player is sent off.
explanation.sayThisLine: Two yellows is a red, one red is off.

payload.prompt: A player keeps fouling every few minutes. What does the referee show?

options.text: Nothing, it's just playing hard
A warning and then a yellow if it continues
A yellow for persistent fouling

explanation.correct: Right. Persistent fouling is a yellow because the referee tells him to stop and he does not.
explanation.incorrect: If a player keeps fouling after being warned, the yellow comes for persistent offences.
explanation.sayThisLine: Foul after foul after foul, that's a yellow.

payload.prompt: A player gets a yellow in the 30th minute and another yellow in the 75th. Is he sent off?

scene.alt: A player receives a yellow card in the first half and another yellow card in the second half of the same match.

explanation.correct: Yes. Two yellows in the same match is a red card and the player is off.
explanation.incorrect: Two cautions in one match result in a red and an immediate sending-off.
explanation.sayThisLine: Two yellows, automatic red, he's gone.

payload.prompt: A player punches an opponent in the face. What does the referee do?

options.text: Shows a yellow card
Shows a red card immediately
Stops the game and talks to him

explanation.correct: Right. Violent conduct is a direct red; he's off immediately without a yellow first.
explanation.incorrect: Any violent act is a straight red card, no warning. That is the most serious offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: Violent conduct, straight red, no yellow.

statement.speaker: Ava
statement.text: That was a red all day. He jumped on him with both feet.

payload.question: What is Ava saying?

options.text: It was a clear red card offense because of violent conduct
The referee should send him off immediately
She thinks he fouled someone
It was just a bad tackle

payload.translation: Ava is saying the player's action was violent and deserves a direct red card dismissal.

followUps.line: Did you see it live or in replay?
followUps.why: Asks where she got the angle.

followUps.line: Do you think VAR would intervene?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: If you're not sure what happened, ask Ava what she saw.

payload.prompt: A player yells at the referee after a decision. What is the card?

options.text: A free kick for the other team
A yellow card for dissent
Nothing, just a warning

explanation.correct: Right. Dissent, arguing with the ref, is a yellow card.
explanation.incorrect: Arguing with the referee or abusing him is a yellow. The captain can speak; others cannot.
explanation.sayThisLine: Can't shout at the ref, that's a yellow.

lessons.title: Advantage and tactical fouls
lessons.objective: You can explain why the referee sometimes lets play run and why fans respect a smart foul.

payload.prompt: A midfielder fouls an attacker, but the attacker's teammate is clean through on goal. Does the ref play advantage?

scene.alt: A foul occurs, but the fouled player's team immediately has a scoring opportunity with an open path to goal.

explanation.correct: Yes. The attacker's team benefits more from playing on than from a free kick.
explanation.incorrect: Advantage means the fouled team gets a better opportunity if play continues, so the ref lets it run.
explanation.sayThisLine: Advantage played, they're in a better position now.

payload.prompt: The ref plays advantage, but the attacking team loses the ball immediately. What happens next?

options.text: The ref stops play and awards the original free kick
Play continues with no free kick
The ref only stops play if there's a foul

explanation.correct: Right. If advantage does not work out, the ref goes back for the original foul.
explanation.incorrect: Advantage can be rescinded; if the fouled team loses the ball quickly, the ref stops and gives the free kick.
explanation.sayThisLine: Advantage play, but if you lose it, he goes back.

payload.prompt: A defender sees a 3-on-1 break, so he trips the attacker. It stops the counter. Does he get a yellow?

scene.alt: With defenders out of position and attackers on a fast break, a defender deliberately fouls to stop the attack and accepts the yellow card.

explanation.correct: Yes. A tactical foul to stop a dangerous counter gets a yellow, and fans respect the trade-off.
explanation.incorrect: A deliberate foul to break up a counter is a yellow card, but it is often praised as smart defending.
explanation.sayThisLine: Smart foul, takes the yellow to stop the goal chance.

payload.prompt: A player jumps and leans into an opponent's shoulder to win a header. Is it a foul or advantage?

options.text: Always a foul, no contact in the air
Only a foul if he uses both arms
Part of the game if both jump for it

explanation.correct: Right. Shoulder-to-shoulder contact when both compete fairly is part of the game.
explanation.incorrect: When both players jump for the ball and use the shoulder fairly, it is legal contest.
explanation.sayThisLine: Both jumped, both fair, no foul.

statement.speaker: Lee
statement.text: Great tactical foul, stopped them on a break for a yellow. That's defending.

payload.question: What does Lee mean?

options.text: The defender deliberately fouled to stop a counter-attack
The defender got a yellow but prevented a goal chance
It was a clean tackle
The defender broke the rules badly

payload.translation: Lee is praising the defender for making a smart calculated foul to prevent a dangerous counter-attack.

followUps.line: Would you take that yellow in that situation?
Do you think VAR should review it?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Tactical fouls are legal; they're just a cost-benefit decision players make.

lessons.title: Last man: DOGSO
lessons.objective: You can explain when a foul is a red card because it denied a goal chance.

payload.prompt: An attacker is through one-on-one with the keeper. The last defender fouls him. What is the card?
payload.context: The fouled player had a clear goal-scoring opportunity with only the goalkeeper to beat.

options.text: A yellow card for the foul
A red card for denying the goal chance
No card, just a free kick

payload.explanation: When the last defender denies a clear goal-scoring opportunity, it is a red card. DOGSO stands for Denying an Obvious Goal-Scoring Opportunity. The rule is: stopping a tap-in chance = red, unless the defender challenges for the ball and there is contact that is careless, in which case it is yellow.
payload.sayThisLine: DOGSO, last man, straight red, no argument.

payload.prompt: The last defender fouls an attacker clean through, but he clearly tried to get the ball. Is it red or yellow?

options.text: Red card, no question
Yellow because he challenged for the ball
Nothing because he tried

explanation.correct: Right. If the defender makes a genuine attempt at the ball, a DOGSO foul is yellow, not red.
explanation.incorrect: DOGSO can be red or yellow: red if it is a blatant denial (no ball attempt), yellow if the defender tried to win it fairly.
explanation.sayThisLine: He went for the ball, so it's yellow not red.

payload.prompt: Two defenders are back. The last one fouls an attacker clear through. Is it DOGSO red?

scene.alt: An attacker is through on goal, but there is a second defender nearby who could also defend. The last defender fouls.

explanation.correct: No. With two defenders back, it is not a clear goal-scoring opportunity; it is not DOGSO.
explanation.incorrect: DOGSO requires the attacker to have a clear, obvious chance. Two defenders means it is not clear, so it is a yellow.
explanation.sayThisLine: Two back, not clear, so it's yellow not red.

payload.prompt: A striker is clean through on goal. A defender fouls him inside the penalty area for a DOGSO. What is the punishment?

options.text: Penalty and red card
Penalty and yellow card
Just a penalty, no card

explanation.correct: Right. DOGSO in the box is a penalty and a red card.
explanation.incorrect: A clear goal-scoring opportunity denied by a foul in the box is a penalty and a red.
explanation.sayThisLine: DOGSO in the box, penalty and red.

payload.prompt: An attacker is clean through. The keeper comes out and fouls him. Is it a red card?

scene.alt: A goalkeeper rushes out of the box and commits a foul on an attacker who is clear through on goal.

explanation.correct: Yes. DOGSO applies to anyone, including the keeper.
explanation.incorrect: Even the goalkeeper can be sent off for denying a clear goal chance by fouling.
explanation.sayThisLine: Keeper fouls clean through, that's a red.

payload.prompt: An attacker has the ball at his feet 15 yards out with one defender between him and goal. Is it DOGSO if fouled?

options.text: Yes, definitely DOGSO
No, too far away and one defender is there
Only if he is on his strong foot

explanation.correct: Right. With a defender between the ball and goal, it is not a clear chance.
explanation.incorrect: DOGSO requires an obvious, clear chance. One defender in the way means it is not clear.
explanation.sayThisLine: One defender in between, it's not clear, so not DOGSO.

lessons.title: Handball, the eternal argument
lessons.objective: You can explain why some handballs are penalties and some are not.

payload.prompt: A defender sees the ball coming and holds out an arm to block it. Handball?

scene.alt: A defender deliberately extends an arm to block or stop a shot or pass heading toward goal.

explanation.correct: Yes. Deliberate use of the hand is handball, no matter the distance.
explanation.incorrect: Any deliberate contact with hand or arm is an offence. Intention is clear here.
explanation.sayThisLine: He put his arm out on purpose, that's handball.

payload.prompt: A cross comes in and hits a defender's arm close to his body. Is it handball?

options.text: Yes, any arm contact is handball
No, the arm is part of the body
Only if the arm moved away from the body

explanation.correct: Right. Natural position is when the arm is close to the body; moving the arm out makes it handball.
explanation.incorrect: The rule is about making your body unnaturally bigger. A natural position is allowed; an unnatural one is not.
explanation.sayThisLine: Arm at the side, probably okay. Arm out, probably handball.

payload.prompt: A defender's arm is at his side. The ball ricochets off his hip and hits his arm by accident. Handball?

scene.alt: A ball deflects unexpectedly and strikes a defender's arm that is in a natural position at the body; contact is incidental.

explanation.correct: No. Accidental contact with the arm in a natural position is not handball.
explanation.incorrect: If the arm is in a natural position and the contact is not deliberate, it is not an offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: Arm at the side, ball hits it by chance, that's not handball.

payload.prompt: The ball hits a player's shoulder. Is it handball?

options.text: Yes, that is the shoulder
No, the shoulder is not the arm
Only if the arm made him bigger

explanation.correct: Right. The shoulder is not the arm. The rule is about hand and arm, and the arm is from the armpit down.
explanation.incorrect: The shoulder is not part of the arm for handball purposes. Contact with the shoulder is not an offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: Shoulder's not the arm, that's not handball.

statement.speaker: Casey
statement.text: His arm made his body bigger, that should be a handball penalty.

payload.question: What is Casey saying?

options.text: The player's arm was in an unnatural position
The enlarged body meant handball
It was accidental so not handball
The arm did not touch the ball

payload.translation: Casey is arguing that the player's arm was not in a natural position, making his body unnaturally bigger, which is handball.

followUps.line: Did the arm move or was it always out there?
followUps.why: Tests understanding of movement vs position.

followUps.line: Would you call that if it was a defender vs a striker?
followUps.why: Notes that handball is applied consistently.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Handball is the most argued rule; both sides usually have a point.

payload.prompt: Handball is called in the penalty area. What is the restart?

options.text: Direct free kick
Penalty kick
Corner kick

explanation.correct: Right. Handball in the box is a penalty.
explanation.incorrect: Any handball in the penalty area is a penalty kick.
explanation.sayThisLine: Handball in the box, straight to the spot.

lessons.title: Diving and dissent
lessons.objective: You can explain why simulation and dissent get cautions.

payload.prompt: A player is lightly brushed and falls down dramatically to win a free kick. What is this?

options.text: A foul on the player
Simulation, a dive; a yellow card
Advantage to the fouled player

explanation.correct: Right. Exaggerating or faking contact to win a free kick is simulation and a yellow.
explanation.incorrect: Simulation is pretending to be fouled when you are not, or exaggerating minor contact. It is an offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: He went down easy, that's a dive, yellow card.

payload.prompt: After the ref makes a call, a player yells 'That was wrong!' and argues with him. Yellow card?

scene.alt: A player loudly disputes a referee decision by arguing or complaining; the player is clearly challenging the referee's authority.

explanation.correct: Yes. Arguing with the referee or abusing him is dissent, a yellow card.
explanation.incorrect: Dissent, arguing with or abusing the referee, is an automatic yellow card offence.
explanation.sayThisLine: Can't argue with the ref, that's a yellow.

payload.prompt: The referee makes a decision. Who is allowed to speak to him about it?

options.text: Any player can ask a question
Only the captain can approach the referee
No one can speak to the ref

explanation.correct: Right. Only the captain or armband holder can speak to the referee.
explanation.incorrect: Only the captain is supposed to talk to the referee about decisions. Others risk a yellow for dissent.
explanation.sayThisLine: Only the captain talks to the ref, that's the rule now.

statement.speaker: Mo
statement.text: He touched him but he went down too easy. That should be a yellow.

payload.question: What does Mo mean?

options.text: The contact was minimal but the player exaggerated
It should be a yellow for simulation or diving
It should be a free kick
The player was seriously fouled

payload.translation: Mo is saying the player exaggerated minor contact to deceive the referee, which is simulation and should be a yellow.

followUps.line: Do you think he went down too easy?
followUps.why: Tests your reading of the contact.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Diving is a judgment call; watch the contact and the fall together.

payload.prompt: A player shoves a referee after an argument. Is he sent off?

scene.alt: A player makes physical contact with a referee, pushing or touching him in aggression.

explanation.correct: Yes. Touching or pushing a referee is violent conduct, a straight red.
explanation.incorrect: Any physical contact with an official is violent conduct and a direct red card.
explanation.sayThisLine: Hands on the ref, that's violent conduct, straight red.

lessons.title: The officials and the keeper's rules
lessons.objective: You can name the officials and explain the back-pass and eight-second rules.

payload.prompt: Match the official to the job.

pairs.definition: The main official who makes decisions, blows the whistle and issues cards.
Two officials on the touchlines who flag for out-of-play and offside decisions.
At the bench who manages substitutions, replacement balls and keeps time.
In a room with screens who can recommend reviews for serious errors.

explanation.summary: Five officials: ref, two assistants on the lines, fourth at the bench, and VAR in a room.
explanation.sayThisLine: One ref, two assistants, fourth official, and VAR.

payload.prompt: A teammate deliberately kicks the ball back to the goalkeeper and he catches it. What does the referee do?

options.text: Nothing, he is allowed to do that
Gives an indirect free kick to the other team
Gives a penalty

explanation.correct: Right. A keeper cannot handle a deliberate back-pass; an indirect free kick is given.
explanation.incorrect: The back-pass rule forbids the keeper from handling the ball if a teammate deliberately kicks it to him.
explanation.sayThisLine: Can't pick up a back-pass, he has to use his feet.

payload.prompt: A goalkeeper catches the ball and holds it. How many seconds can he hold it before it becomes a corner?

explanation.correct: Right. Eight seconds is the limit; a visible five-second countdown shows at the end.
explanation.incorrect: The goalkeeper has eight seconds maximum. After that, the other team gets a corner.
explanation.sayThisLine: Eight seconds and the ref counts down with his hand at the end.

payload.prompt: A free kick is awarded. How far must the defending wall stand from the ball?

options.text: 5 yards
10 yards (9.15 metres)
15 yards

explanation.correct: Right. 10 yards or 9.15 metres is the minimum distance.
explanation.incorrect: Defenders must stand at least 10 yards (9.15 metres) from the ball at a free kick.
explanation.sayThisLine: Wall's got to be ten yards back, standard.

payload.prompt: A throw-in is taken. The ball goes back to the goalkeeper. Can he catch it?

options.text: Yes, throw-ins are not part of the back-pass rule
No, the back-pass rule applies to throw-ins too
Only if he is outside the box

explanation.correct: Right. The back-pass rule only applies to deliberate kicks, not throw-ins.
explanation.incorrect: A throw-in to the keeper is allowed; the back-pass rule covers only deliberate kicks from teammates.
explanation.sayThisLine: Throw-in to the keeper is fine, different rule.

payload.prompt: What does the fourth official do during the match?

options.text: Makes offside calls on the touchline
Manages substitutions, replacement balls and timekeeping
Reviews VAR decisions

explanation.correct: Right. The fourth manages the bench, subs and equipment.
explanation.incorrect: The fourth official stands at the bench, manages substitutions, keeps time and handles spare balls.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fourth official is at the bench, handles the subs and the ball.

lessons.title: Time-wasting crackdown
lessons.objective: You can explain the new restart countdown and injury rules.

payload.prompt: A team is delaying a throw-in. The ref shows a five-second countdown. What happens after?

options.text: The ref waits longer
Possession goes to the other team or a corner is awarded
The ref shows a yellow card

explanation.correct: Right. After the five-second countdown, the other team gets possession or a corner.
explanation.incorrect: A five-second visual countdown is given for delayed throw-ins and goal kicks; if time runs out, possession or a corner goes to the other team.
explanation.sayThisLine: Five-second countdown and if they're still stalling, possession to the other side.

payload.prompt: A player is treated on the field for an injury. Can he go right back on the field?
payload.context: A player receives medical attention on the pitch after an injury and the treatment is completed.

options.text: Yes, he can play immediately
No, he must stay off for at least one minute
He must do a fitness test

payload.explanation: A player who is treated on the pitch must stay off the field for at least one minute after play restarts (a 2026/27 rule clarification). This helps protect player welfare.

payload.prompt: A goalkeeper is slow on a goal kick, and the ref starts the countdown. When does the countdown start?

options.text: Immediately when play stops
After a warning from the ref
When the goalkeeper picks up the ball

explanation.correct: Right. The ref warns first, then shows the countdown.
explanation.incorrect: A warning is given first; then the five-second countdown is shown visually.
explanation.sayThisLine: Warning, then countdown, that's the new rule.

payload.prompt: A substitution is being made. Can the old rule still apply where players walk slowly off?

scene.alt: A player is substituted; the departing player walks slowly toward the touchline instead of leaving quickly.

explanation.correct: No. The new rule wants substitutions to be faster; stalling can now get a countdown.
explanation.incorrect: Substitutes are expected to leave the field quickly now; delay can result in a countdown and possession change.
explanation.sayThisLine: Substitutes have to leave faster now, no more stalling.

payload.prompt: A player has a head injury and is treated on the field. He wants to stay on. What happens?

options.text: He can stay if he feels okay
He must come off for at least one minute
The team gets extra subs for injury

explanation.correct: Right. After on-field treatment, he sits out at least one minute. Safety first.
explanation.incorrect: A treated player must remain off the field for at least one minute to protect player welfare.
explanation.sayThisLine: Treatment on the field, then off for at least a minute.
